registers.role: outcomes and treatment (tax return information: income components and the inputs to the simulated marginal tax rates); sample frame

registers.name_in_paper: the Integrated Database for Labor Market Research (IDA)

linkages: Individual-level dataset constructed by Statistics Denmark linking tax return information to socioeconomic variables for the full Danish population since 1980
Married individuals are linked to spouses: the tax simulator accounts for the jointness of Danish income tax liability (transferable exemptions)

sample.universe: The full Danish population since 1980; the tax simulator and the estimation sample cover 1984-2005
sample.unit_of_observation: individual x three-year interval (base year s to year s+3), stacked over base years 1984-2002
selection_rules: Only taxpayers also observed in year s - 1 (this year is used to construct pre-reform income controls)
Individuals whose income in base year s comes primarily from welfare benefits are excluded
Only people who are fully tax liable in Denmark

Regression-specific: labor income regressions restrict to individuals with positive labor income; capital income regressions drop individuals with zero capital income and those whose capital income changes sign between base year and post year
sample.period: 1984-2005 (tax simulator and estimation); data from 1980 used for pre-reform income controls
sample.n_observations: About 49 million stacked three-year differences before restrictions; about 37 million after the sample restrictions (37,599,492 in Table A1)

construction_notes: Marginal tax rates are not observed and are simulated with the authors' own Danish tax simulator, by increasing a given income component by DKK 100 and taking the change in tax liability divided by 100
Virtual income y = sum_j tau_j z_j - T(z_1,...,z_n), a generalization of standard virtual income to multidimensional income
Instruments: mechanical (simulated) post-reform marginal net-of-tax rates and virtual income under pre-reform (base-year) behavior; three-year log changes of these are used as instruments
Monetary values in real 2005 Danish kroner (DKK); US$1 = 5.6 DKK as of August 2013
Capital income is taken in absolute value and negative and positive capital income are estimated in separate regressions, because the log-linear specification does not allow nonpositive values

Taxable income is defined as personal income + capital income + stock income - deductions (Table 1); in Table 8 the taxable income outcome is described as labor income + other personal income + capital income - deductions
Regressions are weighted by income (labor income, capital income, broad income or taxable income depending on the outcome)
Taxpayers close to kink points are defined as those within 5,000 DKK of the top kink, 3,000 DKK of the middle kink, or 2,000 DKK of the bottom kink
Pre-reform income controls: no controls; log base-year income; ten-piece spline in log base-year income; or ten-piece splines of log s-1 income plus the log deviation between s-1 and s incomes
